title: First session, forward
description: One forward pass over the four families an RPG session touches first — economy, roster, expeditions, progression — using only routes that already have E2E coverage, so a failure is the SHAPE under test and not an unrelated missing route. Every step names the HTTP route it will call; the runner refuses a step whose declared route is not the one it calls.

clock.note: No server clock seam exists yet (RS3 is gated on world-continuity's hibernation-clock), so the server's clock is whatever the host machine's is. Every verdict says so, and every `*Utc`/`*At` field is excluded from the digest by name for exactly this reason — a timestamp reading here measures the machine, not the feature.

rules: The runner may sequence and read; it may not compute. No domain math lives in the runner, and no scenario step computes a value.

Every verdict is a read-back through the same GET route the web FE calls (docs/contributing/live-probe-standard.md section 3). A call response body is captured for SEQUENCING only — an id a later step addresses — never as evidence.
Every subject is created by a real route a real player could have used; a scenario may skip tedium, never a service, a validation or a write.

The squad the expedition fights with must be asserted to be the roster this run built (the fabrication line: WebMatchService.BuildSquad falls back to a Synthetic squad on an empty roster, src/FusionRpg.Server/WebMatchService.cs:570-574).
notes: GET /api/souls/{playerId} and GET /api/souls/{playerId}/ledger are the only routes under /api/souls — there is NO player-facing award route (src/FusionRpg.Server/SoulEndpoints.cs:11). The award step therefore uses the sanctioned SIM seeding surface POST /api/test/seed-souls-demo, which performs the real RpgStore.AwardSouls write with reason 'seed'. Earning souls through a real match before a roster exists is not an option: an empty roster fields the Synthetic squad, which is exactly the fabrication this scenario must not inherit. Filed as RS-F1 in tasks/rpg-simulator-todo.md.

The expedition is made due by MOVING THE CLOCK, not by rewriting a row (RS3 increment 5b, owner ruling on RS-F16 candidate 2). The step below declares an absolute offset of 1860 s from the machine clock; the host applies it through the one seam (FusionRpg.Core.Time.ServerClock) — in-process in place, or by rebooting the real process on the same data dir — and the expedition dispatched at t with due = t + 30m is then due at t + 31m. The SIM-only timer rewind (POST /api/test/expedition-due -> RpgStore.ForceExpeditionDue's UPDATE of due_utc) is RETIRED by the same change: no store bypass replaces it, and the route no longer exists. A host that cannot be told the clock (the CLI's --base-url lane, or any host with no clock control) REFUSES this run by name rather than silently ignoring the declaration.

The digest names only readings this scenario believes are run-stable (a terminal state, a tier, a row id, the run game). The values that depend on the two server-minted RNG seeds — the summon roll (src/FusionRpg.Server/CreatureEndpoints.cs:96) and the expedition seed (src/FusionRpg.Server/ExpeditionEndpoints.cs:36) — are ASSERTED by expect.* rules (closed vocabularies, attribution, the fabrication line) and deliberately not digested, because no scenario can own those seeds yet. The double-run falsifier is what measures the remainder; see RS-F4 in tasks/rpg-simulator-todo.md.

The soul ledger's reasons are asserted as 'every row names one' (allNonEmpty), never as a membership list. Two attempts at a list failed for the same reason: the reasons are the server's own closed vocabulary (~24 members, SoulEarnPolicy.Reasons), so a corpus enumerating the ones it expects is asserting a POPULATION — and the battle's kill earn appeared under load, which the list did not carry. The expedition row's presence is not asserted either: RpgStore.Expeditions.cs:311 writes it only when EventSouls > 0, and that roll is server-minted (RS-F4). What is asserted: this player's rows, non-zero deltas, the seed award present, and the fabrication line on the squad.

RS-F27 policy (measured 2026-09-25): an empty read.progression.ledger is a legal outcome, so this scenario does not add an unconditional notEmpty guard. RpgXpAwardMap.FromActivity returns the player award for a normalized defeat and an empty award list for victory or stalemate; web-mode progression also skips the PvZ plant/zombie awards. A real defeat therefore has a conditional non-vacuity floor, checked from the normal GET read-backs by the focused RS-F27 in-process test; a victory or stalemate may legitimately read zero rows. The 20-run measurement and its exact outcome/ledger observations are recorded in tasks/reports/resume-13-rpg-simulator-rsf27-20260925.md. The current file has no outcome override, and the expedition seed is still minted by the server, so the sample did not cover the full result vocabulary; that limitation is reported rather than filled with fabricated rows.

steps.why: The subject of every later read-back. A player row IS a save, so its empires are seeded in the same transaction.
Funds the summon through the sanctioned SIM seeding surface — see the first note.
The balance route the web FE calls.
The award must be visible on the same GET the web FE calls.
The balance read back is the balance of the player this run created, not the server's current-player fallback.
Builds the roster the expedition must later fight with — the real summon route, which spends souls through the one economy.
The roster read-back. Its instance ids become the squad, so 'the squad came from the roster' is checkable against a route a player uses.

The summon asked for TEN (`count: 10`, the only other legal value being 1 -- src/FusionRpg.Data/Sqlite/RpgStore.Summons.cs:34) and the roller produces exactly `count` results, one specimen minted each (src/FusionRpg.Core/Creatures/SummonRoller.cs:67-77, then the mint loop at src/FusionRpg.Data/Sqlite/RpgStore.Summons.cs:102-117). So the roster must hold at least ten, and this proves it: a pointer that selects nothing returns null and `notEmpty` fails, so an index at 9 is an existence proof for ten elements. `notEmpty` on `$.items` -- what this step used to assert -- would have passed if the route delivered ONE, and an empty roster is still the one input that would make BuildSquad fabricate a squad instead of reading this roster.
Seals the squad + seed. The store validates every id against the roster (squad.unknown-specimen) and the contract gate, so a successful dispatch is itself roster evidence.
The clock is an INPUT (RS3 increment 5b): scout-30m's due time is dispatch + 30 minutes, so declaring the host 31 minutes ahead makes the expedition due without touching due_utc. See the second note.

Resolves the real battles through WebMatchService.RunPlannedMatchAsync and the real BattleEngine, then applies rewards in one state-gated transaction. The captured run ids are what the read-backs below must find.
The expedition row the web FE reads: terminal state, tier, and the squad that actually went out.
Collect is exactly-once and terminal.
The row the read-back found is the expedition this run dispatched, not another one.
A persisted empty squad would make the fabrication assertion below pass vacuously.

THE FABRICATION LINE. The persisted squad must be exactly the roster ids this run read back and handed to dispatch — never a squad the server invented. Dispatch itself refuses an id the roster does not own (squad.unknown-specimen), and this compares the read-back row against the read-back roster rather than against what the runner sent.
Every id the expedition fought with is still an id in the roster this run built.
The battles collect reported must be real webrpg runs, read back through the run list.
An expedition that resolved no battle is not the shape this scenario claims to exercise.
The runs in the list are THIS expedition's (correlation `exp:{id}:{n}`, src/FusionRpg.Server/ExpeditionEndpoints.cs).
The runs are webrpg runs — the one web-match pipeline, not a legacy engine path.
The emitter's closed outcome vocabulary (BattleReportEmitter's `match.result` mapping). The OUTCOME itself is RNG-dependent, so the rule is pinned, never a value.
The run list holds exactly the runs collect reported — the write and the read agree.
The progression summary the web FE reads.
Two read-backs, one subject — read-back compared to read-back, never to a constant the scenario wrote.
The XP ledger the battle's spawn facts must have reached.

Web-mode rule, read back: a webrpg run never levels a PvZ almanac TYPE row (RpgStore.Progression.cs:80 — `!pvzGame` skips every award that is not Player or Species). The ROW SET is outcome-dependent by design, so the rule and the attribution are pinned, never a count.
Every credited row belongs to this run's player.
Every credited row is attributed to a run this expedition actually produced.
A credit with no stated reason is an unattributable change to a save.
The one soul ledger the award, the summon spend and the expedition reward all land in.
The ledger read back is this player's.
The award is visible in the ledger, not only in the balance.

EVERY ROW NAMES A REASON — the rule this corpus can hold still, and the same one it already applies to the XP ledger (`expect.progression.reason`). An enumeration of the reason set was tried first and is the wrong shape: the reasons are the server's own closed vocabulary (`SoulEarnPolicy.Reasons`, ~24 members with the PvZ-activity, contract, respec and run-completion families), so listing the ones a run 'should' produce is asserting a POPULATION (validation-ssot.md), and it was measured failing under load when the battle's own kill earn appeared — `$.items[*].reason is ["expedition","defeat","kill","discovery"×10,"summon","seed"]`, measured 2026-09-23 (full E2E project, 4 m in, `kill` from the activity-fact path `RpgStore.Souls.cs:139`). What IS asserted about these rows: they belong to this player (`expect.souls.ledger.player`), every delta is non-zero (`expect.souls.ledger.deltas`), and the seed award is present (`expect.souls.ledger.seed`). The expedition row's PRESENCE is deliberately not asserted either: the event-souls roll is server-minted (RS-F4) and RpgStore.Expeditions.cs:311 writes the row only when `EventSouls > 0`.
A zero-delta ledger row is a write that changed nothing.

The readings this scenario believes are run-stable: a terminal state, a tier, a row id, and the run engine. Everything RNG-derived is asserted by the expect.* rules above and deliberately left out — see the third note.
